assigned.title: The commander's qualification evidence is collected by hand, one command at a time
assigned.acceptance:
PW-0504 is the OBSERVATION and stays blocked on hardware. This is the PREPARATION, which is engineering, and gpt-architect's round-115 section 4 asks for it by name: 'First prepare the smallest deterministic qualification package/checklist... Prepare this so Diego's part is minimal.'

TODAY THE RUN SHEET ASKS THE COMMANDER TO TYPE POWERSHELL AND PASTE OUTPUT. Step 0 alone is three separate snippets plus two settings pages read by eye, and every later row asks him to notice and copy something. Each hand-copied field is a field that can be wrong, missing, or from the wrong machine, and 'a RIG pass on unrecorded hardware is not evidence' is this document's own rule.

REQUIRED: one command Diego runs AFTER installing and launching, which collects everything collectable without him transcribing anything -- the environment block the matrix specifies (Windows build, GPU and driver, WebView2 runtime, display, audio), the installed tree's location and whether verify-install accepts it, whether sidecar.log exists with its size and tail, whether a liberty-desktop.exe process and its node.exe child are running, and whether the handshake line is present in the log.
REQUIRED: it writes ONE file he sends back, and prints a short human summary so he can see whether it worked before sending it.
REQUIRED: ABSENCE IS RECORDED, NOT SKIPPED. A missing sidecar.log, an unresolvable WebView2 version or a process that is not running are findings the report must state explicitly -- the run sheet already says an absent log is itself a finding, and a collector that silently omitted it would undo that.
REQUIRED: IT CLAIMS NOTHING IT CANNOT SEE. It must not report that WebView2 rendered the application, that playback worked, or that the window appeared. Those are the commander's eyes and the report must say so where it would otherwise be read as covering them. gpt's round-105 section 9: do not collapse those claims.
REQUIRED: NO SECRETS. It must not capture the launch token, environment dumps, or anything from the handshake line beyond host and port.
REQUIRED: testable off Windows. Every platform fact arrives through an injected reader, the way installed-identity.mjs takes `env` as a parameter, so the composition and the absence-handling have a suite on this machine. The Windows commands themselves cannot be executed here and that limit is stated rather than glossed.
REQUIRED: the run sheet's Step 0 and its report format point at the command instead of listing snippets to retype, and the rows only a person can judge stay a person's.

OUT OF SCOPE: marking any PW-0504 row passed. This task delivers the collector; the evidence is still the commander's to produce.
assigned.notes:
FILED ROUND 115 under gpt-architect's instruction to minimise the commander's work before asking for it. The one-command shape is chosen because the alternative already exists and is the problem: the run sheet is correct and it is long, and length is what makes a qualification session get abbreviated.

Scope held deliberately narrow. This does not automate judgement -- G1's compositing result, G2's scaling, the SmartScreen wording, whether a window actually appeared -- only the facts a machine can read about itself.

unit.evidence:
node --test scripts/windows/qualify.test.mjs: 18 tests, 18 pass, 0 fail. node --check clean. repo:validate passed. node --test scripts/assert-no-row-runs-nowhere.test.mjs: 14/14, unaffected.

THE FIX, AND IT IS NOT A REDACTOR. gpt-architect's finding was correct: sidecarLog returned tail: text.slice(-LOG_TAIL_BYTES), which put whatever happened to be in the log -- a token in a URL, an argv, an environment dump -- into a file written to be pasted into a chat. The tail is GONE. In its place, classifyLog() reads the same 16 KiB window and reports ONLY which entries of a fixed signature table matched, plus line and byte counts.

AN ALLOWLIST, NOT A DENYLIST, and that choice is the substance of the fix. Redacting things that "look like secrets" cannot work, because a secret is whatever happened to be in that file and no pattern enumerates it. So nothing the log said can reach the report: the report can only say which of ten patterns written in this repository matched, which is a fact about the table rather than about the file. Each pattern carries a plain-English `means` written here for a reader who has the report and not the machine -- which is the diagnostic value the raw tail had, minus the bytes. The ten: port-in-use, address-unavailable, permission-denied, file-missing, module-missing, module-format, native-module-failed, node-not-found, unhandled-error, fatal.

THE DANGEROUS FAILURE MODE OF AN ALLOWLIST IS HANDLED AND TESTED. A real error nobody wrote a signature for returns an empty list, which reads like "no problem". The note distinguishes them in those words -- "NO RECOGNISED FAILURE SIGNATURE in the examined window. That is not the same as 'no error'" -- it names the file to edit, and it points at the log on the machine, so nothing diagnostic is lost; it just does not travel unless the commander chooses to send it.

THE TEST THE REVIEWER ASKED FOR, AND WHY TWO TESTS THAT EACH LOOKED RIGHT LEFT THE LEAK UNCOVERED. There were already two: one asserted the fixture secret was absent from JSON.stringify(log.handshake) -- one subtree of the returned object -- and one asserted the WHOLE report was clean but fed sidecarLog a CLEAN log fixture. Between them, neither could ever have seen the tail. Now: the fixture hides the same string in THREE places, including an argv line and a URL inside an error line that the handshake logic never looks at; the sidecarLog test asserts on JSON.stringify(log) entire; and the existing full-report test was STRENGTHENED to use that adversarial fixture rather than a second near-duplicate test being added beside it. Both also assert that no raw log line, no URL from the log and no "[out]" prefix reaches the report, and the human-readable summarise() output is checked too, because that is what actually gets pasted.

SIX MUTANTS, ALL CAUGHT: (1) restoring tail: text.slice(-LOG_TAIL_BYTES); (2) adding a "harmless" lastLine field; (3) having the classifier quote the line it matched; (4) deleting the module-format signature from the table; (5) softening the no-signature note to "Nothing to report."; (6) making the examined window unbounded. All six reverted, 18/18 green afterwards. Mutant 4 is caught by a new test that drives one sample line through every pattern in the table, because a table nobody checks grows a dead entry.

docs/WINDOWS_CERTIFICATION.md no longer tells the commander the report carries the log's tail, states that it never quotes sidecar.log, and says why an allowlist rather than a redactor.

A SECOND DEFECT FOUND WHILE FIXING THE FIRST, REPORTED RATHER THAN FIXED, AND IT IS ARGUABLY THE WORSE OF THE TWO: scripts/windows/qualify.test.mjs RUNS NOWHERE. It is not in package.json's test:scripts, and no workflow invokes it -- grep across package.json and .github/workflows finds only test-lifecycle.mjs under scripts/windows. So this task's `unit` gate is a suite that executes only when someone types the command by hand, and the leak was caught by a human reading the code rather than by the suite, which would not have run in any case. I have NOT fixed it: package.json and the workflows are outside this task's allowedPaths, and widening a reviewed surface mid-cycle is the thing the path lock exists to prevent. PL-0730 -- "test:scripts and the CI validate job can disagree in one direction without anything noticing" -- is where it belongs, and it is currently deferred behind PL-0736. Flagging it in the handoff.

STATED, NOT GLOSSED, and unchanged from round 1: none of the PowerShell in qualify.mjs has been executed. Every reading is a Windows fact and this container is Linux. What is proven here is the composition, the absence-handling, the bounding and now the sanitisation, all through injected readers.

OUT OF SCOPE AND NOT DONE: no PW-0504 row is marked passed, and no Windows runtime pass is claimed -- the reviewer's instruction and the position this task has held since round 1. This delivers the collector; the evidence is still the commander's to produce.

review.evidence: CHANGES_REQUESTED, transcribed verbatim in substance from gpt-architect's own message committed to this repository at coordination/agent-bus/gpt-to-claude/MSG-20261008T083807000Z-changes_requested-a741c0de.json (commit 71de85f), which binds itself to commitSha 846a1f4 and baseSha bab637f. THE FINDING: PL-0741's Windows qualification collector emits an unsanitized raw sidecar.log tail despite its NO SECRETS acceptance. sidecarLog() returns tail: text.slice(-LOG_TAIL_BYTES); the fixture embeds secretish:'must-not-appear' in the handshake yet checks only JSON.stringify(log.handshake), not JSON.stringify(log) or the full report. Therefore the test passes while report.sidecarLog.tail contains the test secret. ASKED FOR: return to IN_PROGRESS for a correction -- remove or safely sanitize the raw tail, retain diagnostic absence/error categories, and assert the fixture secret does not appear anywhere in the full serialized report. Do not claim any Windows runtime pass. I AGREE WITH THIS FINDING AND IT IS MINE TO HAVE MISSED: the test asserted on one subtree of the object the collector returns rather than on the object, so it proved the handshake was clean while the tail beside it carried the same bytes. Evidence cited by the reviewer: scripts/windows/qualify.mjs#L190-L235 and scripts/windows/qualify.test.mjs#L115-L131, both at 846a1f4.

assigned.title: Three e2e assertions describe a home page that no longer exists, and two of them never run
assigned.acceptance:
MEASURED FROM THE REAL RUN LOGS, run 38268425224, at 7a43a0cbcc6349eb1943443b10b4b3e0a90bba19. [chromium] tests/critical-journey.spec.ts:114 the home route is served Expected: "One place. Fast playback. Clear decisions." Received: "Deep Current" 19-23 x locator resolved to

Deep Current

[chromium] tests/critical-journey.spec.ts:876 the player page offers a way back same pair THE DEFECT IS NOT THE STRING. Wave 132 (PL-0760) made the home hero LOADER-DRIVEN so the first screen can state a fact about this installation instead of a fixed sentence. These two tests pinned that sentence, and the comment above the first one stated the reason it was safe to pin: "the hero is static markup rendered by the page itself, ABOVE the boundary the catalog load sits inside". That premise is now false. Correcting the assertion and leaving the sentence would have left a comment that lies about why the test exists, which is worse than the failure. REQUIRED: THE INVARIANT ASSERTED MUST BE ONE EVERY BRANCH CAN SATISFY. The hero has four branches -- a spotlight title, an empty cause, a recognised error reason, an unrecognised one -- and no string is common to them. What is common is 200 and EXACTLY ONE h1: a page with none gives a screen reader nothing to land on, a page with two has no single title. It must be held from the other side as well, by a unit test that drives every branch, or the e2e assertion is satisfiable by a page with the wrong heading. REQUIRED: THE THIRD ASSERTION, WHICH DID NOT FAIL AND IS STILL WRONG. The refused branch of "which catalog the home route can serve" matches /couldn.t load the catalog/i. `catalogErrorCopy` now maps `catalog_source_not_configured` to "No catalog source is configured"; "We couldn't load the catalog" survives only as the fallback for a reason this build does not recognise. That branch is skipped in the development configuration, and the production and fail-closed configurations could not start their web server because the build was broken -- so it did not fail, and it would have failed on the next green build. Fixing it in the same change as the two that did fail is the point: a round that fixes only what the log printed leaves the next failure for the next round. MUST NOT: pin another build-dependent string, weaken an assertion to a status code or a `toHaveCount(0)` that an empty page would satisfy, or delete a test. Each correction must be shown to be necessary -- the old assertion must be demonstrated to fail against the current build, not assumed to.
assigned.notes: FILED 2026-10-12 from GitHub Actions run 38268425224 (CI) at 7a43a0c. Sibling of the typecheck regression recorded against PL-0759.

e2e.evidence:
E2E at e0bd80796467f2b6fdd13e0bd35cf198a8092146. EXECUTED IN A REAL BROWSER AGAINST A REAL SERVER IN BOTH CONFIGURATIONS, not reasoned about. development mode, --project=api --project=chromium: 122 passed, 31 skipped, 0 failed (2.6m) production / fail-closed mode (no database, as CI's failclosed step runs it): 71 passed, 82 skipped, 0 failed (47.6s) critical-journey.spec.ts alone: 10/10 development, 10/10 production e2e harness typecheck (the e2e-typecheck job): exit 0 CI at 7a43a0c ran 120 passed + 2 failed in development mode. The 122 here are that same set, now all passing. THE TWO THAT FAILED, verbatim from run 38268425224: critical-journey.spec.ts:114 the home route is served -- Expected "One place. Fast playback. Clear decisions.", Received "Deep Current", 23 x locator resolved to

Deep Current

critical-journey.spec.ts:876 the player page offers a way back -- the same pair, 19 x Both pinned a hero sentence that PL-0760 deliberately replaced with loader-driven copy. The first test's comment also asserted the premise that made pinning safe -- "the hero is static markup rendered by the page itself, ABOVE the boundary the catalog load sits inside" -- and that is now false, so it was rewritten. Leaving a true assertion beside a false explanation is the defect class this project keeps removing. WHAT REPLACES THEM IS AN INVARIANT ALL FOUR BRANCHES CAN SATISFY: 200 and exactly one h1. There is no string common to a spotlight title, an empty cause, a recognised error reason and an unrecognised one. One h1 is a real property -- none gives a screen reader nothing to land on, two gives the page no single title -- and it is NOT asserted only here: apps/web/src/components/home/home-ui.test.tsx's "exactly one h1, in a hero-shaped slot" drives every branch of the component, so the e2e assertion cannot be satisfied by a page with the wrong heading while that unit test holds. The back-to-catalog test asserts the URL plus one h1, because its claim is the navigation, not the destination's wording. THE THIRD CORRECTION IS THE ONE THAT DID NOT FAIL, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-FIX ROUND. The refused branch of "which catalog the home route can serve" matched /couldn.t load the catalog/i. catalogErrorCopy in spotlight.ts maps catalog_source_not_configured to "No catalog source is configured"; the old wording survives only as the fallback for a reason this build does not recognise. Matching it therefore asserted the opposite of that branch's whole point, which is that a refused source is NAMED rather than lumped in with every other failure. It stayed green because the branch is skipped in the development configuration and the two configurations that run it could not start their web server -- the build was broken by the typecheck defect recorded against PL-0759. It would have failed on the next green build. MUTANT RUN, because a correction nobody can show was necessary is a guess: restoring /couldn.t load the catalog/i fails "which catalog the home route can serve is decided by the build, and both are asserted" in production mode -- 1 failed, 9 passed, expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed. Reverted. THE THREE "fail-closed guard" ANNOTATIONS WERE A CONSEQUENCE, NOT A SEPARATE DEFECT, and I checked rather than assuming. The guard reported that "refuses honestly rather than showing an empty list", "publishes nothing only a resolver could know" and "fails closed with 503 and names the operator's remedy" were absent from the report entirely -- renamed or deleted. All three exist: the first in e2e/tests/watchlist.spec.ts, the other two in e2e/tests/playback-session.api.spec.ts. They were absent because their configuration's web server never started, so zero tests ran ("fail-closed suite expected=0 unexpected=0") and the guard correctly failed closed. All three RAN AND PASSED in the production-mode run above (watchlist.spec.ts:315, playback-session.api.spec.ts:830 and :847). Nothing was changed for them, and the guard needs no change: it did exactly its job. ENVIRONMENT NOTE, stated because it bounds what these numbers prove. The sandbox has Playwright browser build 1194 preinstalled; this harness pins @playwright/test 1.62.1, which looks for build 1234's headless shell, so an unmodified run fails 69 tests in 1-11ms each on "Executable doesn't exist" before any page loads. That is an environment mismatch, not a product failure. The runs above used a temporary config that extends e2e/playwright.config.ts and overrides only launchOptions.executablePath; it was deleted afterwards and nothing committed under e2e/ was changed for it. These results are therefore evidence about this harness and this application on Chromium 1194, on Linux. Windows desktop e2e (CI's e2e-desktop job, which reported expected=120 unexpected=2 at 7a43a0c for the same two assertions) still requires the real runner. typecheck gate: npx tsc --noEmit -p e2e exit 0; the repository's own npm run typecheck (turbo, whole repo) exit 0 at this commit.

assigned.title: Nothing anywhere proves the packaged application STARTS, only that it is served
assigned.acceptance:
THE GAP, AND IT IS WHY FOUR CONSECUTIVE ROUNDS SHIPPED A BROKEN INSTALLER WITH GREEN CHECKS.

packaged-server-smoke.mjs boots the packaged sidecar and fetches `/`. Since Wave 131A it also requires the application frame's markers and refuses the error headline. All of that is necessary and NONE of it executes JavaScript. The Wave 132 failure is a TypeError thrown while a client module is being EVALUATED -- the report's frames resolve to the Turbopack ESM instantiation chain -- and a fetch of server-rendered HTML cannot observe that at any cost. The HTML was always correct. The application never started.

REQUIRED: THE PACKAGED ARTIFACT IS RUN IN A REAL BROWSER. Relocated outside the repository, booted with a real sidecar token, and driven with a real engine that evaluates the client bundle. Nothing less can see a module-evaluation failure.

REQUIRED: THREE INDEPENDENT CHANNELS, EACH ABLE TO FAIL ALONE, because the recurring defect class here is a check whose shape an absence satisfies.
  (1) THE DOM: the frame's markers present AND no boundary headline present. Either half alone is satisfiable by a failure -- markers-only passes a page that rendered then threw, headline-only passes a blank page.
  (2) pageerror: an uncaught exception reaching the window, which a module-evaluation throw produces BEFORE any boundary exists to catch it.
  (3) THE DIAGNOSTICS ROUTE: a POST to /api/v1/diagnostics/client-failure means a boundary fired and reported, in the same vocabulary the operator's log will carry.
A pass requires all three clean. The self-test below demonstrates that they are genuinely independent rather than three spellings of one check.

REQUIRED: A SELF-TEST THAT INVERTS THE SCRIPT. It injects a module-evaluation TypeError and requires the script to FAIL. A qualification test nobody has shown can fail is a green light with no lamp in it, and this project has already shipped three of those.

REQUIRED: THE SCRIPT STATES WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, in its output and not only in a comment. It runs Chromium. The installed application runs WebView2 inside the Tauri shell, and the Wave 132 failure reproduces there and not under Chromium -- so a pass means "the packaged bundle starts under Chromium", never "the MSI starts". Claiming otherwise would be the fabrication the operating contract forbids by name.

REQUIRED: AN ABSENT BROWSER IS A SKIP WITH EXIT 2, NOT A PASS. e2e/ is deliberately outside the workspaces so a browser download is not a prerequisite of npm ci; a qualification script that silently passes when it could not launch anything is worse than one that is not run.

MUST NOT: be wired into a workflow file in the declaring round -- .github/workflows/ci.yml, windows.yml and desktop-shell-ci.yml are all reserved by tasks in REVIEW. The script must therefore be runnable by one documented command, and the fact that nothing schedules it yet must be reported rather than implied away.
assigned.notes: FILED 2026-10-13 after the operator's installed MSI at faa6e8a failed to start while CI, Windows package and the packaged smoke were all green.

implementationBaseProvenance.reason: The script was written and committed before the task was filed, because the task's acceptance is derived from what the operator's crash report proved about the gap -- that nothing executes the client bundle -- and that was only established by resolving the three turbopack frames. faa6e8a is the commit the installed MSI was built from and the last commit before any of this script exists.

integration.evidence:
INTEGRATION at b14848c4978f96d8ae700158fdc95a885f09f1f5. EXECUTED AGAINST THE PACKAGED ARTIFACT IN A REAL BROWSER, both ways.

NORMAL RUN -- node apps/desktop/scripts/packaged-startup-qualification.mjs, 8 checks, all passed:
  ok  the packaged tree was relocated outside the repository
  ok  the relocated sidecar starts and announces a port (bound 43217)
  ok  the packaged homepage answers 200 (16461 bytes)
  ok  the application frame rendered (carries skip-link, class="shell", id="main")
  ok  no error boundary is on screen (neither "could not start this page" nor "Something went wrong")
  ok  the home page rendered exactly one h1
  ok  no uncaught exception reached the window (pageerror never fired)
  ok  no client failure was reported (no POST to /api/v1/diagnostics/client-failure)

SELF-TEST -- the same script with --self-test, which injects a module-evaluation TypeError and requires the script to FAIL. It failed, as required:
  FAIL  no uncaught exception reached the window
        TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'selfTest')
  SELF-TEST PASSED: the injected module-evaluation TypeError was detected.

AND THE SELF-TEST TAUGHT SOMETHING THE DESIGN ONLY ASSERTED. Of the three channels, ONLY pageerror caught the injected failure. The DOM channel stayed clean (the application still rendered, because the injected throw was not in the app's own graph) and the diagnostics channel stayed clean (no boundary fired). That is the empirical proof that the three channels are independent rather than three spellings of one check -- and it means a single-channel version of this script, which is what a first draft would have been, would have passed the injected failure.

WHAT EACH CHECK WOULD STILL BE SATISFIED BY, stated because that question is what this project's last four regressions turned on:
  - "answers 200" alone: an error page, a 404 body, an empty body. Which is why it is never alone.
  - "frame rendered" alone: a page that rendered the shell and then threw during hydration.
  - "no boundary headline" alone: a blank page, a 404, a network failure.
  - "exactly one h1" alone: an error boundary, which also renders exactly one h1. Deliberately so -- that is why it sits beside the headline check rather than replacing it.
  - pageerror alone: a failure React caught and reported without ever reaching the window.
  - the diagnostics POST alone: a failure that threw before any boundary existed to report it -- which is precisely the Wave 132 case.
No single check is load-bearing. All three channels must be clean.

A MISSING BROWSER IS A SKIP WITH EXIT 2 AND SAYS SO IN WORDS ("THIS IS A SKIP, NOT A PASS: nothing was qualified"), because e2e/ is deliberately outside the workspaces and a browser is not guaranteed present. A script that silently passes when it could not launch anything is the failure mode this task exists to remove, in a new place.

ENVIRONMENT, stated because it bounds the claim: run under Chromium build 1194 via LIBERTY_QUALIFICATION_CHROMIUM, resolving Playwright from e2e/node_modules. The script prints, on every run, that it does NOT prove WebView2 compatibility.

NOT SCHEDULED BY ANYTHING YET. .github/workflows/ci.yml and windows.yml are reserved by PL-0736 and desktop-shell-ci.yml by PL-0746, both in REVIEW, so wiring this into a job would collide with a reserved surface. The one place that currently executes scripts on windows-latest is package-sidecar.mjs, which is PL-0755's surface and has been reopened four times already. So this round delivers the script and one documented command, and the fact that nothing runs it automatically is a known limitation rather than an omission.
